visuals.title: Where SARS-CoV-2 hits
visuals.text: Mainly the lungs, but ACE2-rich tissues elsewhere and the clotting system are involved too.

visual.title: Chest X-ray
visual.caption: Bilateral infiltrates, often peripheral and lower zone.

glossary.Respiratory infection: An infection of the airways or lungs.
glossary.droplets: Tiny drops of fluid from coughing or sneezing that carry germs a short distance.
glossary.Transmitted: Passed from one person to another.
glossary.Risk factors: Things that make a disease more likely or more severe.
glossary.chronic lung disease: Long-term lung conditions such as COPD, asthma or pulmonary fibrosis.
glossary.Obesity: Excess body fat, usually defined as a BMI of 30 or more.
glossary.Immunosuppression: A weakened immune system, from disease or from drugs such as steroids or chemotherapy.
glossary.URTI: Upper respiratory tract infection: infection of the nose, sinuses or throat, like a common cold.
glossary.Viral pneumonia: Infection of the lung tissue itself caused by a virus.
glossary.Respiratory failure: The lungs cannot keep blood oxygen high enough or carbon dioxide low enough.
glossary.Dry cough: A cough that brings up no sputum.
glossary.Shortness of breath: Feeling unable to get enough air; also called dyspnoea.
glossary.Fatigue: Persistent tiredness and lack of energy.
glossary.Crackles: Fine crackling sounds heard with a stethoscope when fluid or inflammation fills the small airways.
glossary.Pulmonary embolism: A blood clot that has travelled to and blocked an artery in the lungs.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available, against which others are judged.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment that relieves symptoms while the body fights the illness itself.
glossary.Paracetamol: A simple painkiller that also lowers fever.
glossary.Supplemental oxygen: Extra oxygen given through a mask or nasal tubes.
glossary.Antiviral: A drug that stops a virus from multiplying.
glossary.Ventilation: Mechanical breathing support, where a machine moves air in and out of the lungs.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Treatment with drugs that reduce blood clotting.
glossary.Prophylactic: Given to prevent a problem rather than treat one.
glossary.Hospitalised: Admitted to hospital as an inpatient.
glossary.Respiratory distress: Visible struggling to breathe: fast breathing, use of accessory muscles, inability to speak in sentences.
glossary.Respiratory epithelial cells: The cells lining the airways and alveoli.
glossary.Receptor: A protein on a cell surface that a molecule or virus binds to.
glossary.Immunomodulatory: Altering or calming the immune response.
glossary.Diffuse alveolar damage: Widespread injury to the air sacs, the tissue pattern seen in ARDS.
glossary.Alveolar: Relating to the alveoli, the tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens.
glossary.Inflammatory: Relating to inflammation, the body's response to injury or infection.
glossary.Endothelial injury: Damage to the inner lining of blood vessels, which encourages clotting.
glossary.Viral RNA replication: The virus copying its RNA genetic material to make new viruses.
glossary.Metabolism: The body's chemical breakdown of a drug, mostly in the liver.
glossary.Cytokine: A signalling protein released by immune cells that drives inflammation.
glossary.Corticosteroid: A steroid hormone drug that suppresses inflammation, such as dexamethasone.
